newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks finished weaker on Thursday, unable to sustain Wednesday's bull run on the back of Wall Street without fresh local news from either government or the Reserve Bank, dealers said.
"It wasn't able to follow through from yesterday when it advanced on the back of Wall Street," said David Shapiro of Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Dealers added that some profit-taking was seen as short-term players cashed in after the industrial index finished Wednesday at a new high of 9,032.3.
Some good buying was seen at these lower levels and dealers said institutions were accumulating stock.
"We saw purchases at these cheaper levels. That's where there were some big trades," one dealer said.
Stock moved back into the local market in the form of basket selling from London professionals and this provided liquidity.
The local market was awaiting any news from either government or Reserve Bank to give it direction, dealers said.
"This trend is difficult to sustain without news. It's looking for the government or the bank to say something," Shapiro said.
Stocks were seen building support at these levels before testing upside again.
Industrials finished more or less flat while golds slipped to close weaker after the struggling bullion price eroded the ground from underneath them.
Overall volumes were hefty with more than a billion rands worth of shares traded on the day.
The Industrial index finished 6.0 points down at 9,026.3, golds fell 29.8 to 952.6 and all-shares were dragged 19.9 points down to 7,427 points.
South African financial services company Sage Group Ltd enjoyed heavy volumes traded in a number of bookovers done by broker SMK Securities Ltd, dealers said.
Dealers said the volumes could be related to a possible buyout by Samgro Investment Holdings Ltd.
Sage closed 30 cents down at 25.70 rand after touching a day's high of 26.25 rand.

Carrig Diamonds Ltd finished as the biggest percentage gainer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange after it said earlier it planned to dispose of its shareholding in wholly-owned subsidiary Rex Mining Corp (Rexcor) for cash to its Canadian controlling shareholder Rex Diamond Mining Corp.
Carrig will then distribute approximately 90 percent of its cash resources to Carrig shareholders by way of a reduction in the share premium account.
Carrig finished 38 cents higher at 110 rand in a volume of 93,400 shares.
After opening firmer near-term share futures were weaker in late trade, although dealers said the underlying mood was strong.
The September all-share contract was at 6,690/700 from 6,721, the industrial contract is at 8,581/88 from 8,617 and the gold contract is at 665/72 from 695.
-- Melanie Cheary, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482 1003
